question: What is the typical timeframe for the onset of an immediate drug reaction?

options.D: Within minutes to a few hours

explanation: Immediate reactions are characterized by their rapid development shortly after the causative agent enters the body. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h1)

question: Why is early recognition of acute drug hypersensitivity particularly critical in busy outpatient settings?

options.A: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing replacement drugs
options.B: It guarantees the patient will develop lifelong drug tolerance
options.C: It prevents rapid progression to life-threatening multi-organ failure
options.D: It eliminates the need for any subsequent medical documentation

explanation: Because these reactions escalate swiftly, catching them early stops the cascade before it becomes fatal. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h1)

question: Which specific antibody class is primarily responsible for mediating Type I immediate hypersensitivity reactions?
explanation: Type I reactions rely on IgE antibodies attaching to mast cells and basophils to trigger allergic mediator release. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h2)

question: What physiological event immediately follows the cross-linking of cell-bound antibodies by a triggering drug?

options.A: Degranulation and release of stored inflammatory mediators
options.B: Immediate proliferation of circulating red blood cells
options.C: Permanent suppression of the bone marrow immune response
options.D: Thickening of the outermost layer of the epidermis

explanation: Cross-linking activates mast cells and basophils to dump powerful chemical mediators like histamine into the tissues. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h2)

question: Which clinical feature distinguishes a moderate drug reaction from a mild one?

options.A: Involvement of mild systemic or respiratory symptoms
options.B: Complete cardiovascular collapse and cardiac arrest
options.C: Delayed onset occurring five days after administration
options.D: Total absence of any cutaneous skin manifestations

explanation: Mild reactions stay localized to the skin, whereas moderate reactions introduce systemic features like mild breathing difficulty. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h3)

question: A patient presents with localized itching and mild rash on the arm thirty minutes after an antibiotic injection, with normal vital signs. How should this reaction be classified?
explanation: Localized skin changes without systemic, respiratory, or hemodynamic compromise fall into the mild category. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h3)

question: What is the most characteristic respiratory sign of upper airway laryngeal edema during anaphylaxis?
explanation: Laryngeal swelling narrows the upper airway, producing a high-pitched sound known as stridor. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h4)

question: Which combination of hemodynamic and respiratory findings indicates severe systemic anaphylaxis?
explanation: Anaphylaxis compromises both circulation through vasodilation and ventilation through airway constriction. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h4)

question: What is the very first action a nurse must take when a patient develops an acute adverse drug reaction to an IV infusion?

options.C: Document the exact time in the chart

explanation: Ceasing further exposure to the causative agent is the mandatory first step in managing any acute reaction. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h5)

question: Why is the ABCDE framework utilized during the rapid assessment of a suspected severe drug reaction?

options.A: It provides a legal record for pharmaceutical manufacturers
options.B: It prioritizes the immediate identification of life-threatening organ system failures
options.C: It calculates the financial cost of emergency antidotes
options.D: It determines the exact chemical formula of the offending drug

explanation: The ABCDE approach ensures airway, breathing, and circulation are evaluated and stabilized first. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h5)

question: Which parameter provides the best immediate indicator of tissue oxygenation during an acute drug reaction?
explanation: Pulse oximetry gives a continuous, non-invasive measurement of how well oxygen is circulating in the blood. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h6)

question: What clinical significance does a persistently rising respiratory rate hold during the monitoring phase of an allergic reaction?

options.A: It is a harmless artifact caused by the blood pressure cuff
options.B: It proves the patient is responding positively to therapy
options.C: It often signals impending respiratory fatigue and deterioration
options.D: It indicates that normal homeostatic balance has returned

explanation: Tachypnea is an early compensatory response to hypoxia and bronchospasm before oxygen levels crash. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h6)

question: What is the primary first-line pharmacological treatment for severe anaphylaxis?
explanation: Epinephrine is the essential first-line drug that rapidly counteracts both airway constriction and vascular collapse. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h7)

question: A patient experiencing severe anaphylactic shock with profound hypotension should ideally be positioned in which posture while awaiting emergency response?

options.A: Upright in a high Fowler position
options.B: Prone with the head turned sideways
options.C: Flat on the back with legs elevated
options.D: Sims position resting on the left side

explanation: Elevating the legs helps maximize venous return to the heart and maintain cardiac output during shock. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h7)

question: Which national regulatory body is responsible for receiving adverse drug reaction reports in Nigeria?
explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control oversees pharmacovigilance and drug safety reporting in Nigeria. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h8)

question: Why is detailed post-reaction documentation and allergy labeling critical for patient safety?

options.A: It removes all legal liability from the attending medical team
options.B: It allows the pharmacy to automatically issue monetary refunds
options.C: It prevents accidental re-administration of the same offending drug
options.D: It fulfills a purely cosmetic requirement for hospital archives

explanation: Clear charting and prominent allergy alerts ensure that healthcare providers avoid prescribing or giving the trigger agent again. [learn more](GNS215_U5_T4#GNS215_U5_T4_h8)
